question: We can add a table in an MS Word document from which of the following tabs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Insert Tab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Insert tab in MS Word contains the Tables group, which lets users insert a table into a document by specifying the number of rows and columns, or by drawing one manually. (टेबल सम्मिलित करना — इन्सर्ट टैब)

 

• The Insert tab also houses other object-insertion tools such as Pictures, Shapes, SmartArt, Charts, Header & Footer, and Hyperlinks.

 

• The Home tab primarily deals with text formatting (font, paragraph, styles, clipboard), not object insertion.

 

• The Design tab is used for applying themes, colours, and page borders/watermarks to the overall document appearance, not for inserting objects.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Insert tab ribbon in MS Word is typically organised into groups: Pages, Tables, Illustrations, Add-ins, Media, Links, Comments, Header & Footer, Text, and Symbols.

 

NOTE

 

• View Tab (Option 1): Controls how the document is displayed, e.g. Print Layout, Read Mode, Zoom, and split-window options — not for inserting content.

 

• Home Tab (Option 2): Contains basic formatting tools like Font, Paragraph, Styles, and Clipboard — no table-insertion tool.

 

• Design Tab (Option 3): Applies document-wide themes, colours, fonts, and page background/watermark settings — not for inserting tables.

question: In which year was the first underground section (Vishwavidyalaya- Kashmere Gate) of the Golden Route opened in New Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2004.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first underground section of the Delhi Metro, between Vishwavidyalaya and Kashmere Gate, was opened in the year 2004, as part of Phase I of the network. (दिल्ली मेट्रो — भूमिगत खंड, 2004)

 

• This underground stretch forms part of what is today the Yellow Line of the Delhi Metro, connecting north Delhi with the walled-city area.

 

• The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) was incorporated in 1995, and the first (elevated) section of the network, Shahdara to Tis Hazari, had opened on 25 December 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Delhi Metro Phase I (2002-2006) covered parts of the Red, Yellow, and Blue lines and was a landmark in urban mass-transit development in India.

 

• E. Sreedharan, popularly called the "Metro Man of India," led DMRC's construction during this phase.

 

NOTE

 

• 2000 (Option 2): Construction of the Delhi Metro network had not yet begun; DMRC's first line opened only in December 2002.

 

• 1997 (Option 3): DMRC had only recently been incorporated (1995); no line was operational this early.

 

• 1998 (Option 4): Still within the pre-construction/early-construction phase of the Delhi Metro project.

question: Name the digital payment platform launched in 2021 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in association with Department of Financial Services (DFS), National Health Authority (NHA) and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW).
solution_text:
The correct answer is e-RUPI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• e-RUPI is a cashless, contactless digital payment platform in the form of a prepaid e-voucher, launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) in association with the Department of Financial Services (DFS), National Health Authority (NHA), and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), and was officially launched by the Prime Minister on 2 August 2021. (ई-रूपी — डिजिटल भुगतान प्लेटफॉर्म)

 

• It is a QR code or SMS string-based e-voucher delivered to a beneficiary's mobile phone, redeemable at specific service providers without needing a card, digital payments app, or internet banking access.

 

• It was initially used to ensure leak-proof delivery of welfare services, including payments for COVID-19 vaccination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• e-RUPI runs on the UPI (Unified Payments Interface) platform and was built by NPCI in partnership with banks.

 

• It aims to promote person- and purpose-specific digital payments in sectors like health, education, and fertiliser subsidies.

 

NOTE

 

• MobiKwik (Option 1): A private digital wallet and payments company, unrelated to this government-backed voucher launch.

 

• Dhani (Option 3): A private fintech app offering loans, payments, and healthcare services, not a government e-voucher platform.

 

• YONO (Option 4): "You Only Need One" is State Bank of India's digital banking platform, not an NPCI e-voucher initiative.

question: Which Article of the Constitution mentions that “the Parliament consists of the President and two Houses known as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha)”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 79.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 79 of the Indian Constitution establishes the Parliament, stating that "There shall be a Parliament for the Union which shall consist of the President and two Houses, to be known respectively as the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha)." (अनुच्छेद 79 — संसद का गठन)

 

• Article 79 falls under Part V (The Union), Chapter II (Parliament) of the Constitution.

 

• The President, though not a member of either House, is an integral part of Parliament since presidential assent is required for a bill to become law.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 80 deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha, and Article 81 deals with the composition of the Lok Sabha.

 

• Article 83 prescribes the duration of the Houses of Parliament (the Lok Sabha's normal term is five years; the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body that never fully dissolves).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 82 (Option 1): Deals with readjustment of seats in the House of the People after each census.

 

• Article 70 (Option 3): Deals with discharge of the President's functions in other contingencies not provided for elsewhere in the Constitution.

 

• Article 73 (Option 4): Deals with the extent of executive power of the Union.

question: Which of the following statements best describes the Hardy Schulze rule?
option_1: The ions are removed from the solution by the phenomenon of diffusion through a permeable membrane.
option_2: The partial pressure of a component in a liquid mixture is proportional to its mole fraction in that mixture.
option_3: This is applied to obtain a colloidal solution of metals such as gold, silver or platinum.
option_4: The amount of electrolyte required for the coagulation of a definite amount of a colloidal solution is dependent on the valency of the coagulating ion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The amount of electrolyte required for the coagulation of a definite amount of a colloidal solution is dependent on the valency of the coagulating ion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hardy-Schulze rule (also called the Schulze-Hardy rule) states that the coagulating/precipitating power of an electrolyte for a colloidal solution depends on the valency of the ion carrying a charge opposite to that of the colloidal particle — the greater the valency of the coagulating ion, the greater its coagulating power. (हार्डी-शुल्ज नियम — विद्युत-अपघट्य आयन की संयोजकता)

 

• This means the amount of electrolyte required to coagulate a given colloidal solution decreases as the valency of the coagulating ion increases, exactly as described in option 4.

 

• For example, for a negatively charged colloid (like an As₂S₃ sol), coagulating power follows the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This principle explains coagulation values (flocculation values) — the minimum concentration of an electrolyte required to cause coagulation of a colloidal sol within a given time.

 

• Coagulation of a colloidal sol can also be achieved by other methods such as boiling, electrophoresis, and mixing two oppositely charged sols.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Describes dialysis, a purification method for colloids using a semi-permeable membrane, unrelated to the Hardy-Schulze rule.

 

• Option 2: Describes Raoult's law, relating partial pressure to mole fraction in a solution, not a coagulation rule.

 

• Option 3: Describes peptization, the process of converting a freshly formed precipitate into a colloidal solution, not the Hardy-Schulze rule.

question: What was the name of Swami Vivekanand’s guru?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramakrishna Paramhansa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Vivekananda's spiritual guru was Ramakrishna Paramhansa, a mystic and priest associated with the Kali temple at Dakshineswar, near Kolkata. (रामकृष्ण परमहंस — विवेकानंद के गुरु)

 

• Vivekananda (born Narendranath Datta) became his chief disciple, and after Ramakrishna's death in 1886, founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 to carry forward his teachings.

 

• Vivekananda represented Hinduism at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, delivering his famous "Sisters and Brothers of America" address.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January, Swami Vivekananda's birthday.

 

• Ramakrishna Paramhansa's teachings emphasised the harmony of all religions ("as many faiths, so many paths").

 

NOTE

 

• Swami Ram Singh (Option 1): Founder of the Namdhari (Kuka) Movement among Sikhs, unrelated to Vivekananda.

 

• Swami Dayanand (Option 2): Founder of the Arya Samaj in 1875, a separate 19th-century reform movement.

 

• Aadi Shankaracharya (Option 3): An 8th-century philosopher who propounded Advaita Vedanta; not Vivekananda's guru.

question: The Green Revolution was due to the introduction of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is high yielding varieties of seeds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution in India, led by Dr. M. S. Swaminathan (building on techniques developed by Norman Borlaug), was primarily driven by the introduction of High Yielding Varieties (HYV) of seeds, especially of wheat and rice. (हरित क्रांति — उच्च उपज देने वाली किस्मों के बीज)

 

• It began in the mid-1960s and was concentrated initially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Alongside HYV seeds, the revolution also relied on increased use of chemical fertilisers, irrigation, and pesticides, but the seeds are regarded as its defining technological input.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. M. S. Swaminathan is known as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India."

 

• The Green Revolution helped make India self-sufficient in foodgrain production, reducing its dependence on imports such as PL-480 wheat from the US.

 

NOTE

 

• Irrigation (Option 1): An important supporting input, but not the defining innovation of the Green Revolution.

 

• Fertilisers (Option 2): Used alongside HYV seeds, but not the central technology that defines the Green Revolution.

 

• Fisheries (Option 4): Unrelated to the Green Revolution, which focused on foodgrain crops; the corresponding development in fisheries/aquaculture is called the "Blue Revolution."

question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam is a famous dancer of _______ dance form of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam was a renowned exponent and choreographer of Kuchipudi, a classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh. (कुचिपुड़ी नृत्य — वेम्पति चिन्न सत्यम)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising Kuchipudi worldwide and establishing the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai in 1963 to train dancers systematically.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1998) for his contribution to Indian classical dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kuchipudi traditionally originated as a dance-drama performed by Brahmin men in the village of Kuchipudi, and later evolved to include solo and female performances.

 

• Other famous Kuchipudi exponents include Yamini Krishnamurthy and Raja and Radha Reddy.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 1): Classical dance form of Tamil Nadu; famous exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Manipuri (Option 2): Classical dance of Manipur, known for its Raas Leela performances.

 

• Odissi (Option 3): Classical dance of Odisha, associated with gurus such as Kelucharan Mohapatra.

question: The famous book ‘Sangraha Choodamani’, which deals with the current system of Carnatic music was written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Govindacharya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Sangraha Choodamani' is a Sanskrit treatise dealing with the melakarta (parent-scale) system of Carnatic music, and is attributed to Govindacharya. (संग्रह चूड़ामणि — गोविंदाचार्य)

 

• The text is significant because the 72 melakarta scheme currently followed in Carnatic music is largely based on the system laid out in this work, building on the earlier framework of Venkatamakhin.

 

• It systematically names and organises the 72 parent ragas (melakartas) from which other ragas (janya ragas) are derived.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The melakarta system groups the 72 parent scales into 12 chakras (groups of six), each named using the Katapayadi sankhya numbering scheme.

 

• Venkatamakhin's 17th-century text "Chaturdandi Prakashika" laid the theoretical foundation later expanded in Sangraha Choodamani.

 

NOTE

 

• Damodara Misra (Option 1): Author of the "Sangita Darpana," another treatise on Indian music, but not of Sangraha Choodamani.

 

• Matanga (Option 2): Author of "Brihaddesi," an ancient treatise credited with an early elaboration of the term "raga."

 

• Haripala (Option 3): Author of "Sangita Sudhakara," a medieval work on music, unrelated to Sangraha Choodamani.

question: Kiran Nadar was conferred with the highest civilian award of which country in April 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kiran Nadar, philanthropist and founder of the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art (KNMA), was conferred with France's highest civilian award, the Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur (Knight of the Legion of Honour), in April 2023. (शेवेलिए दे ला लीजियन डी'ऑनर — किरण नादर, फ्रांस)

 

• The honour was awarded in recognition of her contribution to promoting art and culture, including strengthening cultural ties between India and France.

 

• The Légion d'Honneur was instituted by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1802 and remains France's highest order of merit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indians honoured with the Légion d'Honneur include Ratan Tata, Amitabh Bachchan, and Shah Rukh Khan.

 

• Kiran Nadar is the wife of Shiv Nadar, founder of HCL Technologies.

 

NOTE

 

• Poland (Option 2), Egypt (Option 3), Germany (Option 4): None of these countries conferred this particular civilian honour on Kiran Nadar in April 2023; the award in question was specifically conferred by the French Republic.

question: What do you mean by semiconservative DNA replication?
option_1: After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have two parental and two newly synthesised strand.
option_2: RNA is dependent on DNA for the synthesis of proteins
option_3: DNA is dependent on RNA for the synthesis of proteins
option_4: After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Semiconservative DNA replication means that after replication is complete, each of the two resulting DNA molecules consists of one original (parental) strand and one newly synthesised strand. (अर्ध-संरक्षी प्रतिकृति — एक पैतृक, एक नई श्रृंखला)

 

• This model was experimentally confirmed by the classic Meselson-Stahl experiment (1958), using E. coli grown first in heavy nitrogen (¹⁵N) and then in normal nitrogen (¹⁴N) medium.

 

• During replication, the DNA double helix unwinds, and each of the two parental strands acts as a template for synthesising a new complementary strand, resulting in two "hybrid" daughter molecules.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The two other proposed models of DNA replication were conservative (the parental double helix stays fully intact, an entirely new copy is made) and dispersive (both strands of both daughter molecules are a patchwork of old and new segments) — both were ruled out by the Meselson-Stahl experiment.

 

• DNA polymerase is the key enzyme responsible for synthesising the new strand during replication.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Describes a conservative model of replication (two fully parental + two fully new strands), which was experimentally disproved.

 

• Options 2 and 3: Describe the relationship between RNA and DNA in protein synthesis (transcription/translation), not the mechanism of DNA replication at all.

question: The colour of the surface of Mars is red because of the presence of large amounts of chemical compounds in it. What is the name of that compound?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron oxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reddish colour of Mars, which earns it the nickname "the Red Planet," is due to the presence of large quantities of iron oxide (Fe₂O₃, commonly known as rust/hematite) in its soil and rocks. (मंगल ग्रह — आयरन ऑक्साइड)

 

• Iron minerals on the Martian surface oxidised over billions of years, giving the planet its characteristic rusty-red appearance.

 

• Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the solar system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos.

 

• Notable Mars missions include India's Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission), launched in 2013, making India the first Asian nation to reach Martian orbit.

 

NOTE

 

• Tin oxide (Option 1): Not associated with Mars' surface colour.

 

• Magnesium oxide (Option 3): Present in small amounts in Martian rocks, but not responsible for its red colour.

 

• Nitrogen oxide (Option 4): Not a significant component of Mars' surface composition or its characteristic colour.

question: In MS-Word, a number printed above the base line is called ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is superscript.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS Word, a character or number printed slightly above the normal line of text (the base line) is called superscript — commonly used for exponents (like x²) or footnote markers. (सुपरस्क्रिप्ट — बेसलाइन से ऊपर)

 

• The keyboard shortcut to apply superscript formatting in MS Word is Ctrl + Shift + Plus (+).

 

• Superscript formatting is available in the Font group of the Home tab.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The opposite formatting, where text appears slightly below the base line (e.g., in chemical formulas like H₂O), is called subscript, applied with Ctrl + Equal-sign (=).

 

• Both superscript and subscript are commonly used for scientific and mathematical notation within word processors.

 

NOTE

 

• Strikethrough (Option 2): Formatting that draws a line through the middle of text, used to indicate deleted content — unrelated to base-line position.

 

• Above BL (Option 3): Not standard MS Word terminology; a distractor option.

 

• Subscript (Option 4): The opposite formatting — text printed below, not above, the base line.

question: How many censuses had been completed in India as of year 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Census of India 2011 was the 15th Census conducted in India since census-taking began, the first synchronous all-India census having been held in 1881. (जनगणना 2011 — 15वीं जनगणना)

 

• Census 2011 was also the 7th census after independence (1951, 1961, 1971, 1981, 1991, 2001, 2011).

 

• The theme of Census 2011 was "Our Census, Our Future."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 recorded India's population as approximately 121.08 crore, making India the second most populous country in the world at that time.

 

• The Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India during the 2011 Census was C. Chandramouli.

 

NOTE

 

• 12 (Option 1): Understates the total number of censuses conducted since census-taking began in India.

 

• 7 (Option 2): This is the number of censuses conducted only after independence, not the total count since 1881.

 

• 16 (Option 4): Overstates the count; the 16th Census (due around 2021) was postponed and had not been conducted as of the reference date.

question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT vis-à-vis features of the Indian Constitution?

1) Though India has a federal system, the Constitution does not mention the word ‘federation’.

2)Article 5 of the Constitution says that the Parliament by law can create a new state.

3) On the subjects in the Union list, each State Legislature can enact laws for the State.

4)Both the Parliament and State Legislature can pass laws on subjects in concurrent list.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Although India has a federal structure, the Constitution never uses the word "federation"; instead, Article 1 describes India as a "Union of States." (भारतीय संविधान — राज्यों का संघ)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect: It is Article 3, not Article 5, that empowers Parliament to form new states, alter boundaries, or change the names of existing states by law. (Article 5 actually deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.)

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: On subjects in the Union List, only Parliament can enact laws; State Legislatures cannot legislate on Union List subjects (except in specific circumstances such as a national emergency).

 

• Statement 4 is correct: Both Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on subjects placed in the Concurrent List, though the central law prevails in case of conflict (Article 254).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution divides legislative powers between the Union and the States into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.

 

• India is described as a "Union of States" (rather than a "federation") partly because Indian states cannot secede from the Union, unlike constituent units of a typical federation formed by voluntary agreement.

 

NOTE

 

• Only 1 (Option 3): Incorrectly identifies only statement 1 as incorrect, whereas statement 1 is actually correct.

 

• 1 and 4 (Option 1): Incorrectly includes statements 1 and 4, both of which are factually correct, while missing 2 and 3.

 

• 1 and 3 (Option 2): Incorrectly includes correct statement 1 while correctly flagging only one of the two genuinely incorrect statements.

question: Under which Gharana do the composition of blend of Khayal and Dhrupad-Dhamar styles come?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agra Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Agra Gharana of Hindustani classical vocal music is known for its distinctive style that blends elements of Khayal singing with the older Dhrupad-Dhamar tradition, giving its renditions a robust, rhythmically forceful character. (आगरा घराना — ख्याल और ध्रुपद-धमार का मिश्रण)

 

• It was founded by Ustad Ghagge Khuda Baksh in the 19th century; prominent exponents include Faiyaz Khan and Vilayat Hussain Khan.

 

• The gharana system in Hindustani classical music refers to a lineage-based tradition of musical style and pedagogy, each associated with a particular city.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Khayal gharanas include the Gwalior Gharana (the oldest gharana, often called the "mother" of Khayal gharanas), the Kirana Gharana, and the Patiala Gharana.

 

NOTE

 

• Indore Gharana (Option 1): Founded by Ustad Amir Khan, known for its slow, meditative style.

 

• Gwalior Gharana (Option 3): The oldest Khayal gharana, known for simplicity and balance rather than a Dhrupad-Dhamar blend.

 

• Patiala Gharana (Option 4): Known for its layakari (rhythmic play) and use of light-classical elements like thumri; founded by Ali Bux and Fateh Ali Khan.

question: The number of Indian athletes who participated in the Tokyo Paralympics 2020 was ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 54.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India sent its largest-ever contingent of 54 athletes to the Tokyo Paralympics 2020 (held in 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic), competing across 9 sporting disciplines. (टोक्यो पैरालंपिक 2020 — 54 भारतीय एथलीट)

 

• India won a record 19 medals at these Games — 5 gold, 8 silver, and 6 bronze — its best-ever Paralympic performance up to that point.

 

• Notable gold medallists included Avani Lekhara (shooting, India's first woman to win a Paralympic gold), Sumit Antil (javelin throw), Manish Narwal (shooting), Pramod Bhagat (badminton), and Krishna Nagar (badminton).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tokyo 2020 Paralympics were held from 24 August to 5 September 2021 in Tokyo, Japan.

 

• India's previous best Paralympic performance had been 4 medals, at the 2016 Rio Paralympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 57 (Option 1), 56 (Option 2), 55 (Option 4): These figures do not match India's actual contingent size; the officially confirmed number of Indian athletes at Tokyo 2020 was 54.

question: Which Pala ruler temporarily occupied Kanauj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dharmapala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dharmapala, the second ruler of the Pala dynasty of Bengal, temporarily occupied Kanauj during the prolonged tripartite struggle for control of the Gangetic plains among the Palas, the Gurjara-Pratiharas, and the Rashtrakutas. (धर्मपाल — पाल वंश, कन्नौज)

 

• Dharmapala installed his own nominee, Chakrayudha, as a puppet ruler on the throne of Kanauj after defeating the Pratihara forces there.

 

• He is also remembered for founding the great Buddhist monastic university of Vikramashila.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pala dynasty was founded by Gopala around 750 CE, elected by regional chieftains to end a period of anarchy ("matsyanyaya") in Bengal.

 

• Dharmapala's son and successor, Devapala, further expanded the Pala Empire to its greatest territorial extent.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopala (Option 1): Founder of the Pala dynasty; did not occupy Kanauj.

 

• Devapala (Option 3): Dharmapala's successor, known for expanding Pala territory further, but the temporary occupation of Kanauj is specifically attributed to Dharmapala.

 

• Harapala (Option 4): Not a historical Pala ruler; included here as a distractor option.

question: According to Census of India 2011, what was the sex ratio recorded in the Union Territory of Puducherry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1037 females/1000 males.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Census of India 2011, the Union Territory of Puducherry recorded a sex ratio of 1037 females per 1000 males, one of the highest among Indian states/UTs. (जनगणना 2011 — पुडुचेरी लिंगानुपात 1037)

 

• The all-India sex ratio as per Census 2011 was 943 females per 1000 males.

 

• Kerala had the highest sex ratio among Indian states in Census 2011, at 1084 females per 1000 males.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among Union Territories, Puducherry ranked highest for sex ratio in Census 2011.

 

• Haryana recorded the lowest sex ratio among states in Census 2011, at 879 females per 1000 males.

 

NOTE

 

• 980 (Option 1), 1095 (Option 2), 890 (Option 4): These figures do not correspond to Puducherry's actual sex ratio as per the 2011 Census; the officially recorded figure was 1037.

question: The Ultimate Kho-Kho League was started in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ultimate Kho Kho (UKK) League, a professional franchise-based league for the traditional Indian sport of Kho-Kho, was launched with its inaugural season in 2022. (अल्टीमेट खो-खो लीग — 2022)

 

• The league was established to popularise Kho-Kho on a professional, franchise-based model, similar to leagues like the IPL and the Pro Kabaddi League.

 

• The first season of the Ultimate Kho Kho League featured multiple city-based franchise teams competing in a league format.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kho-Kho is an ancient Indian tag sport; India has also hosted the Kho-Kho World Cup, with its inaugural edition held in New Delhi.

 

• The Kho Kho Federation of India (KKFI) governs the sport at the national level.

 

NOTE

 

• 2020 (Option 1), 2021 (Option 2), 2023 (Option 4): These years do not mark the launch of the Ultimate Kho Kho League, which was actually launched in 2022.

question: Indian Constitution came into force on __________ and is celebrated as Republic Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 26 Jan 1950.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950, a date chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) declaration made by the Indian National Congress on 26 January 1930. (26 जनवरी 1950 — गणतंत्र दिवस)

 

• This day is celebrated every year in India as Republic Day.

 

• The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 (now celebrated as Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas), but it formally came into effect two months later, on 26 January 1950.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

 

• India became a sovereign democratic republic on 26 January 1950, with Dr. Rajendra Prasad as its first President.

 

NOTE

 

• 26 Jan 1951 (Option 1) and 26 Feb 1950 (Option 4): Incorrect dates; the Constitution actually came into force on 26 January 1950.

 

• 26 Jan 1948 (Option 3): India was still a dominion under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, at this time and had not yet adopted its own Constitution.

question: Who among the following launched the digital platform ‘FASTER’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chief Justice of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The digital platform 'FASTER' (Fast and Secured Transmission of Electronic Records) was launched by the Chief Justice of India, then Justice N. V. Ramana, in September 2021. (फास्टर पोर्टल — भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• The FASTER system was introduced by the Supreme Court of India to enable instant, secure electronic transmission of court orders — such as bail orders — directly to prison/jail authorities, preventing delays in the release of undertrials and convicts.

 

• It was introduced in response to concerns over undertrials remaining in custody despite grant of bail, due to delays in physical communication of court orders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• FASTER uses secure electronic communication with digital signatures to transmit certified copies of Supreme Court orders to the relevant authorities.

 

• The system's launch followed high-profile cases where individuals remained in jail despite being granted bail, owing to delays in the physical order reaching the jail.

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister (Option 2), Finance Minister (Option 3), President (Option 4): None of these functionaries launched the FASTER portal; it is a judiciary-specific initiative launched by the Chief Justice of India for the Supreme Court's use.

question: In field hockey, in a penalty stroke, an attacker shoots at goal from _____ yards away in a one-on-one confrontation with the goalkeeper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In field hockey, a penalty stroke is awarded for certain infringements (such as a deliberate foul inside the shooting circle) and is taken by an attacking player from a spot 6.4 metres (7 yards) directly in front of the goal, in a one-on-one confrontation with the goalkeeper. (पेनल्टी स्ट्रोक — 7 गज)

 

• During the penalty stroke, all players other than the striker and the defending goalkeeper must stay outside the 23-metre area, and the goalkeeper must stand on the goal line without moving until the ball is played.

 

• A penalty stroke is a direct shot at goal, unlike a penalty corner, which involves a restart from the backline.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Field hockey is governed internationally by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).

 

• A hockey match traditionally consists of four quarters of 15 minutes each.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 (Option 1), 8 (Option 2), 9 (Option 4): These distances do not match the official rule; the penalty-stroke spot is fixed at 7 yards (6.4 m) from the goal line under FIH rules.

question: Who was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor to the Government of India in the year 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is V Anantha Nageswaran.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Government of India in January 2022, succeeding Krishnamurthy Subramanian. (मुख्य आर्थिक सलाहकार — वी अनंत नागेश्वरन)

 

• As CEA, he heads the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, and is responsible for authoring the annual Economic Survey of India.

 

• Before this appointment, he had earlier served as a part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chief Economic Advisor's post had remained vacant for a period after K. V. Subramanian's term ended in December 2021, before Nageswaran's appointment.

 

• Previous CEAs of India include Arvind Subramanian, Raghuram Rajan, and Kaushik Basu.

 

NOTE

 

• S Somanath (Option 1): Former Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), unrelated to the post of CEA.

 

• Krishnamurthy Subramanian (Option 2): The immediate predecessor of V. Anantha Nageswaran as CEA, whose term ended in December 2021.

 

• R Rangarajan (Option 4): Likely a reference to C. Rangarajan, a former RBI Governor and economist, but he did not serve as CEA in 2022.

question: Which river is known as the sorrow of Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kosi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kosi River, known for its frequent and devastating floods caused by shifting its course across the low-gradient plains of north Bihar, is popularly called the "Sorrow of Bihar." (कोसी नदी — बिहार का शोक)

 

• The Kosi originates in the Himalayas (Tibet/Nepal region) and is a major left-bank tributary of the Ganga, known for carrying a heavy sediment load that causes it to change its channel course dramatically over time.

 

• To control its flooding, the Kosi Barrage was constructed at Bhimnagar (near the India-Nepal border) as part of the Kosi Project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Similarly, the Damodar River was historically called the "Sorrow of Bengal" before dams built by the Damodar Valley Corporation controlled its flooding.

 

• The Kosi river system is formed by the confluence of three rivers — the Sun Kosi, Arun, and Tamur — in Nepal, before entering Bihar.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahi (Option 1): A river flowing through Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Gujarat, draining into the Gulf of Khambhat; not associated with Bihar.

 

• Betwa (Option 2): A tributary of the Yamuna, flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; not associated with Bihar's flood history.

 

• Son (Option 3): A major tributary of the Ganga flowing through Bihar, but it is not the river referred to as the "Sorrow of Bihar" — that designation belongs specifically to the Kosi.
